title: What the first frost does to a leek
excerpt: Our grower called on Tuesday: the cold has come, and the leeks have turned sweet. Why the best week of the year for this dish is the first cold one.
content:
Our grower called on Tuesday. The cold has come to the valley, and the leeks have turned sweet. It happens every year, and every year it changes the menu within a day.

Why cold makes them sweet

A leek protects itself from frost by turning starch into sugar. In the field that is survival. Over a fire it means the outer leaves blacken while the heart goes soft and almost honeyed.

How we cook them

Whole, unwashed, straight onto the embers for twelve minutes. We peel away the burnt layers at the pass and dress what is left with romesco and brown butter. Nothing else.

The dish takes twelve minutes and eleven months of waiting.

Charred leeks are on the menu until the ground thaws. Book a table while they last.
